Traditional Atole

Served at: Dia de los Angelitos

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Atole is a warm, comforting Mexican beverage made from masa (corn dough), flavored with cinnamon and sweetened with piloncillo or sugar. It is traditionally served during Dia de los Angelitos, the first day of Mexico's Day of the Dead celebrations, honoring deceased children with offerings and sweet treats.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) milk
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn flour)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) piloncillo or brown sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine 1 cup (240 ml) of milk with the masa harina and whisk until smooth with no lumps.
  2. Add the remaining 3 cups (720 ml) of milk, piloncillo or brown sugar, cinnamon stick, and a pinch of salt to the saucepan.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly to prevent lumps, until it thickens slightly and becomes creamy, about 15-20 minutes.
  4. Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla extract.
  5. Serve hot in mugs, perfect for warming up during Dia de los Angelitos festivities.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with evaporated milk.
  • You can add a pinch of ground cloves or nutmeg for extra warmth and spice.
  • If masa harina is unavailable, you can use corn starch but the texture will be less traditional.
